Below is an outline of what’s happening and why, followed by the necessary *SEARCH/REPLACE* patches to add a new `light` modifier to the React `<OverflowMenu>` component (so you can render a white menu on a gray background, just like TextInput’s `--light` variant).

1. Bug scenario & root cause  
   - On a light-gray page background, the default Carbon overflow menu is rendered in its standard dark-gray style. This low-contrast menu “blends in” and is hard to see.  
   - Other Carbon components (e.g. TextInput) offer a `--light` variant that inverts or lightens their inner UI. OverflowMenu has no such variant exposed in React, so you cannot toggle it.  

2. Fix strategy  
   - Add a new boolean `light` prop to `<OverflowMenu>` in React.  
   - Emit two new CSS classes when `light` is true:  
     - `bx--overflow-menu--light` on the root trigger wrapper  
     - `bx--overflow-menu-options--light` on the floating `<ul>` menu  
   - Wire these classes up via `classnames`.  
   - Update PropTypes, defaultProps, and (optionally) the Storybook story to expose the knob.
